actions.name: retrieve_price_books
actions.description: Retrieve price books. Retrieve a list of price books available in your HubSpot account. This endpoint supports pagination and can return archived price books if specified. It is useful for accessing and managing pricing information across different products and services.

after.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

archived.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

actions.name: create_price_book
actions.description: Create price book. Create a new price book in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to define custom properties, a name, and supported currencies for the price book. A successful request will return the URL of the newly created resource.

customProperties.description: An object containing custom properties for the price book. Each property is a key-value pair where the key is a string and the value is also a string. This is a required property.

description.description: A description of the price book. This is an optional string property.

name.description: The name of the price book. It is a required string property.

supportedCurrencies.description: An array of strings representing the currencies supported by the price book. This is a required property.

actions.name: retrieve_price_book
actions.description: Retrieve price book. Retrieve a specific price book by its unique identifier in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to access detailed information about a price book, including its status and supported currencies. It can be useful for managing and reviewing pricing strategies within your commerce system.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to retrieve.

archived.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

actions.name: delete_price_book
actions.description: Delete price book. Delete a specific price book from your HubSpot account using its unique identifier. This operation will permanently remove the price book and its associated data, making it unavailable for future use.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to delete.

actions.name: update_price_book
actions.description: Update price book. Update an existing price book in your HubSpot account. This operation allows you to modify details such as the name, description, supported currencies, and custom properties of a price book. It is useful for keeping your price book information up to date with the latest changes.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to update.

customProperties.description: An object containing custom properties for the price book, where each key is a property name and the value is a string.

description.description: An object representing the description of the price book to be updated.

name.description: An object representing the name of the price book to be updated.

supportedCurrencies.description: An array of strings representing the currencies supported by the price book.

actions.name: activate_price_book
actions.description: Activate price book. Activate a specific price book in your HubSpot account. This operation changes the status of the price book to active, allowing it to be used in transactions and other operations. Ensure that the price book ID is correct before activation.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to activate.

actions.name: deactivate_price_book
actions.description: Deactivate price book. Deactivate a specific price book in your HubSpot account. This action changes the status of the price book to inactive, making it unavailable for use in transactions. Use this endpoint when you need to temporarily or permanently disable a price book without deleting it.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to deactivate.

actions.name: list_price_book_items
actions.description: List price book items. Retrieve a list of items associated with a specific price book in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to paginate through the items and specify which properties to include in the response. It is useful for managing and viewing the details of products linked to a particular price book.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to retrieve items for.

after.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

properties.description: A list of property names to include in the response.

actions.name: add_price_book_items
actions.description: Add price book items. Add new items to a specified price book in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to associate products with a price book by providing the necessary product details. It is useful for managing and updating the contents of your price books efficiently.

priceBookId.description: The unique identifier of the price book to which items will be added.

productId.description: The unique identifier of the product to be added to the price book. It is a string and is required.

actions.name: batch_archive_price_book_items

q.description: Filter to dashboards whose name or description contains the search string.

actions.name: create_dashboard
actions.description:
Create dashboard. Creates a new dashboard. Existing reports can optionally be attached to the dashboard at creation time; report widgets will be appended sequentially.

Attaching reports to the dashboard is done on a best-effort basis, and it's possible that some or all reports may fail to be attached. The dashboard will still be created, and no error will be returned. The requestor should check the `widgets` field in the response object to see which reports were successfully attached.

businessUnitId.description: The ID of the business unit to associate the new dashboard with. Optional, the account's default is used by default.

description.description: A description of the new dashboard. Optional.

name.description: The name of the new dashboard.

permissionType.description:
The type of permission to apply to the report. Valid values are:
- PRIVATE: The report is only accessible to its owner and administrators.
- EVERYONE_VIEW: The report is viewable by everyone.
- EVERYONE_EDIT: The report is viewable and editable by everyone.
- SPECIFIC: In addition to the owner, specific users and/or teams are granted VIEW or EDIT permissions. The `specificPermissions` field must also be present.

specificPermissions.description:
Array of specific permission grants. Must be present when `permissionType` is set to `SPECIFIC`, ignored otherwise.

Dashboards can have one or two specific permission configurations: one for VIEW grants and/or one for EDIT grants. Specific users and/or teams receive either VIEW or EDIT permissions based on which configuration they appear in. A given user or team cannot appear in both VIEW and EDIT configurations.

grants.description: An array of grants detailing the users and/or teams to grant the specific permission to. At least one grantee must be specified.

grantType.description: The type of entity to grant permissions to, either `USER` or `TEAM`.

granteeId.description: The ID of the user or team to grant permissions to.

permissionType.description: The type of permission granted, either `VIEW` or `EDIT`.

reportIdsToAdd.description: Array of IDs of reports that should be added to the dashboard after creation. Optional.

actions.name: export_dashboard
actions.description:
Export dashboard. Exports a dashboard's content to one or more HubSpot users via standard HubSpot communication channels (notably, email).

Status tracking is not available; a successful request will result in a `204 No Content` response.

Any set of HubSpot users can be specified as the recipients. However, if a given user does not have access to reporting, does not have CRM export permissions, etc., then they will receive a notification with an error rather than a successful export.

**NOTE: This API can only be called from apps with user-level access.** Attempting to call from an app with account-level access (including legacy apps) will fail, because only real users can request exports.

dashboardId.description: The ID of the dashboard to export.

exportType.description:
The type of export to perform. Valid values are:
- `SCREENSHOT`: Individual report screenshots.
- `PDF`: PDF with individual report screenshots.
- `PPTX`: PPTX with individual report screenshots.
- `ZIP`: ZIP of individual report screenshots.
- `CSV`: ZIP with one or more CSV files per report.
- `XLS`: ZIP with one XLS file per report, each with one or more sheets.
- `XLSX`: ZIP with one XLSX file per report, each with one or more sheets.

message.description: The message to include with the export. Optional, empty by default.

recipientUserIds.description: Array of user IDs to send the export to. If absent or empty, the requesting user is used as the sole recipient; otherwise, this exact set of users is used.

reportIds.description: Array of IDs of reports to optionally narrow the export to. IDs of reports that are not on the dashboard are ignored. If absent or empty, all reports on the dashboard are included.

Add report to dashboard. Adds a single report to a dashboard. The report widget is appended to the end of the existing dashboard layout. If the report is already on the dashboard, does not exist, or the requesting user doesn't have permission to access it, does nothing. Check the dashboard in the response to determine whether the report was successfully added.

Dashboards cannot have more than 50 reports on them; attempting to add beyond that limit will fail.

actions.name: list_favorites
actions.description:
List favorites. Retrieves a list of the requesting user's favorite reports and dashboards.

Favorites are returned sorted according to their display order, and then alphabetically by object name as a tiebreaker (favorites without an explicit display order are placed at the end of the results).

**NOTE: This API can only be called from apps with user-level access.** Attempting to call from an app with account-level access (including legacy apps) will fail.

actions.name: add_favorite
actions.description:
Add favorite. Adds the report or dashboard specified in the request as a favorite for the requesting user. If the specified report or dashboard is already a favorite, the request will succeed, updating the existing favorite's display order if necessary.

A user may have at most 10 favorites for each object type (reports, dashboards); attempting to add more will result in an error. Additionally, the user must have at least VIEW permissions for the target object to favorite it.

**NOTE: This API can only be called from apps with user-level access.** Attempting to call from an app with account-level access (including legacy apps) will fail.

displayOrder.description: A number used to determine where in the overall ordering this favorite should be sorted. Optional; favorites without an explicit `displayOrder` will be last in the favorite list.

objectId.description: The ID of the report or dashboard to favorite.

objectType.description:
The type of object to favorite. Possible values are:
- `DASHBOARD`
- `REPORT`

actions.name: set_favorites
actions.description:
Set all favorites. Replaces all of the requesting user's favorites with the ones specified in the request.

A user may have at most 10 favorites for each object type (reports, dashboards); the entire request will fail if it includes too many favorites for either object type. Additionally, the user must have at least VIEW permissions for the target object to favorite it, or that specific favorite will fail. As a special case, if all requested favorites fail individually, the user's existing set of favorites will remain unchanged.

**NOTE: This API can only be called from apps with user-level access.** Attempting to call from an app with account-level access (including legacy apps) will fail.

actions.description: Create recurring dashboard export. Creates a recurring dashboard export

dashboardId.description: The ID of the dashboard that the recurring export should export.

exportType.description:
The type of export to perform. Possible values are:
- `SCREENSHOT`: Individual report screenshots.
- `PDF`: PDF with individual report screenshots.

- `XLS`: ZIP with one XLS file per report, each with one or more sheets.
- `XLSX`: ZIP with one XLSX file per report, each with one or more sheets.

The ID of the user who should own the recurring export. The export is performed using this user's data permissions.

**Note:** apps with account-level access MUST set this to explicitly specify an owning user. For apps with user-level access, optional; if not specified, the requesting user is used by default. In all cases, the specified user must have at least VIEW permissions on the recurring export's target dashboard.

recipientUserIds.description: Array of user IDs to send the export to.  If absent or empty, the owner user is used as the sole recipient; otherwise, this exact set of users is used.

reportIds.description: Array of IDs of reports on the target dashboard which should be included in the export, if present. All reports on the dashboard are included if absent.

The frequency with which to send the recurring export. Also determines how the `scheduledDays` field is used. One of the following:
- `DAILY`: The export is sent daily at `scheduledHour`. The `scheduledDays` field is not used.
- `WEEKLY`: The export is sent weekly at `scheduledHour`, one or more days of the week. The `scheduledDays` field must be used to specify one or more days.
- `MONTHLY`: The export is sent monthly at `scheduledHour`, one or more days of the month. The `scheduledDays` field must be used to specify one or more days.

scheduledDays.description:

actions.name: batch_archive_reports
actions.description:
Batch archive reports. Archives one or more reports. Already-archived reports are silently ignored. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

Archived reports are purged after 90 days.

inputs.description: Array of report or dashboard IDs.

actions.name: batch_restore_reports
actions.description:
Batch restore reports. Restores one or more archived reports. Already-active reports are silently ignored. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

inputs.description: Array of report or dashboard IDs.

actions.name: batch_update_report_business_units
actions.description:
Batch update report business units. Updates the business unit for one or more reports. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

businessUnitId.description: The ID of the business unit to update to.

inputs.description: Array of report or dashboard IDs.

actions.name: batch_update_report_owners
actions.description:
Batch update report owners. Updates the owner of one or more reports. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

inputs.description: Array of report or dashboard IDs.

ownerId.description: The ID of the user to change the owner to.

actions.name: batch_update_report_permissions
actions.description:
Batch update report permissions. Updates the permissions for one or more reports. The maximum batch size is 500.

If any of the requested items fail, the response code will be `207 Multi-Status` and the response will include details of individual failures.

Note that reports on any dashboards cannot have their permissions updated; they inherit the dashboards' permissions. Attempting to update them will result in an error.

inputs.description: Array of report IDs.

permissionType.description:
The type of permission to apply to the report. Valid values are:
- PRIVATE: The report is only accessible to its owner and administrators.
- EVERYONE_VIEW: The report is viewable by everyone.
- EVERYONE_EDIT: The report is viewable and editable by everyone.
- SPECIFIC: In addition to the owner, specific users and/or teams are granted VIEW or EDIT permissions. The `specificPermissions` field must also be present.

grants.description: An array of grants detailing the users and/or teams to grant the specific permission to. At least one grantee must be specified.

grantType.description: The type of entity to grant permissions to, either `USER` or `TEAM`.

granteeId.description: The ID of the user or team to grant permissions to.

permissionType.description: The type of permission granted, either `VIEW` or `EDIT`.

actions.name: get_report
actions.description:
Get report. Retrieves a single report.

Also supports retrieving archived reports via the `archived` query parameter. Retrieving archived reports requires the requesting user to be the report owner, a reporting admin, or a super admin.

reportId.description: The ID of the report to retrieve.

archived.description: Whether to retrieve an archived dashboard instead of an active one. Default false.

properties.description: Additional properties to include in the response. Valid values are: `dashboardIds`, `permissions`, `tags`.

actions.name: update_report
actions.description:
Update report. Partially updates a report. All fields in the request are optional; only the fields which are present will be updated.

Can also be used to archive or restore a report using the `archived` field. When `archived` is present in a request, it must be the only field present, or it will result in an error. Archived reports are purged after 90 days.

Note that reports on any dashboards cannot have their permissions updated; they inherit the dashboards' permissions. Attempting to update them will result in an error.

reportId.description: The ID of the report to update.

archived.description: Whether to archive (`true`) or restore (`false`) the report. Cannot be combined with any other fields.

businessUnitId.description: The new business unit ID to use for the report. Set to `null` to reset to the account's default business unit. Omit to leave unchanged.

description.description: The new description to use for the report. Set to `null` to clear the description. Omit to leave unchanged.

name.description: The new name to use for the report. Omit to leave unchanged.

ownerUserId.description: The ID of the user to change the report's owner to. Omit to leave unchanged.

permissionType.description:
The type of permission to apply to the report. Valid values are:
- PRIVATE: The report is only accessible to its owner and administrators.
- EVERYONE_VIEW: The report is viewable by everyone.
- EVERYONE_EDIT: The report is viewable and editable by everyone.
- SPECIFIC: In addition to the owner, specific users and/or teams are granted VIEW or EDIT permissions. The `specificPermissions` field must also be present.

grants.description: An array of grants detailing the users and/or teams to grant the specific permission to. At least one grantee must be specified.

grantType.description: The type of entity to grant permissions to, either `USER` or `TEAM`.

granteeId.description: The ID of the user or team to grant permissions to.

permissionType.description: The type of permission granted, either `VIEW` or `EDIT`.

actions.name: export_report
actions.description:
Export report. Exports a report to one or more HubSpot users via standard HubSpot communication channels (notably, email).

Status tracking is not available; a successful request will result in a `204 No Content` response.

Any set of HubSpot users can be specified as the recipients. However, if a given user does not have access to reporting, does not have CRM export permissions, etc., then they will receive a notification with an error rather than a successful export.

**NOTE: This API can only be called from apps with user-level access.** Attempting to call from an app with account-level access (including legacy apps) will fail, because only real users can request exports.

reportId.description: The ID of the report to export.

exportType.description:
The type of export to perform. Valid values are:
- `SCREENSHOT`: Screenshot of the report.
- `CSV`: ZIP with one or more CSV files.
- `XLS`: XLS file with one or more sheets.
- `XLSX`: XLSX file with one or more sheets.

message.description: The message to include with the export. Optional, empty by default.

recipientUserIds.description: Array of user IDs to send the export to. If absent or empty, the requesting user is used as the sole recipient; otherwise, this exact set of users is used.

subject.description: The subject line to use for the export. If absent, the name of the requested report will be used. Max length of 100 characters.

actions.name: create_meeting
actions.description: Create meeting. Create a new calendar meeting event in your HubSpot account. This endpoint allows you to specify details such as the meeting title, start and end times, and associated users. The organizerUserId is required to identify the meeting organizer.

associations.description: An array of associations related to the meeting event, each represented by an ExternalAssociationCreateRequest object.

to.description: Contains the Id of a Public Object

id.description: The unique identifier for the public object. It is a string that serves as a reference to the object within the API.

types.description: An array of association specifications, detailing the types of associations to be created. Each item in the array is an object that defines the association type.

items.description: Defines the type, direction, and details of the relationship between two CRM objects.

associationCategory.description: A string indicating the category of the association. Valid values include 'HUBSPOT_DEFINED', 'USER_DEFINED', 'INTEGRATOR_DEFINED', and 'WORK'.

associationTypeId.description: An integer representing the unique identifier for the type of association.

reminders.description: An array of ExternalReminder objects that specify the timing and frequency of the email reminders.

numberOfTimeUnits.description: The number of time units before the meeting when the reminder should be sent. This is an integer value.

timeUnit.description: The unit of time for the reminder. Valid values include 'WEEKS', 'DAYS', 'HOURS', and 'MINUTES'.

shouldIncludeInviteDescription.description: A boolean indicating whether the invite description should be included in the email reminder.

hs_activity_type.description: The type of activity for the meeting. This is a string value.

hs_attachment_ids.description: An array of strings representing the IDs of attachments associated with the meeting.

hs_attendee_owner_ids.description: An array of strings representing the IDs of the owners of the attendees for the meeting.

hs_internal_meeting_notes.description: Internal notes for the meeting. This is a string value.

hs_meeting_body.description: The body content or description of the meeting. This is a string value.

hs_meeting_end_time.description: The end time of the meeting, in ISO 8601 format.

hs_meeting_location.description: The location of the meeting. This is a string value.

hs_meeting_location_type.description: The type of location for the meeting. Valid values include 'PHONE', 'ADDRESS', and 'CUSTOM'.

hs_meeting_outcome.description: A string representing the outcome of the meeting.

hs_meeting_start_time.description: The start time of the meeting, in ISO 8601 format.

hs_meeting_title.description: The title of the meeting. This is a string value.

hs_timestamp.description: A timestamp indicating when the meeting event was created, in ISO 8601 format.

hubspot_owner_id.description: The unique identifier of the HubSpot owner associated with the meeting.

timezone.description: A string representing the timezone in which the meeting event is scheduled.

duration.description: An integer representing the duration of the meeting in minutes.

email.description: The email address of the person booking the meeting.

firstName.description: The first name of the person booking the meeting.

formFields.description: An array of form fields filled out by the participant, each containing a name and value.

name.description: The name of the form field, represented as a string.

value.description: The value associated with the form field, represented as a string.

lastName.description: The last name of the person booking the meeting.

legalConsentResponses.description: An array of legal consent responses, each detailing the consent given by the participant.

communicationTypeId.description: A string representing the unique identifier for the type of communication for which consent is being recorded.

consented.description: A boolean indicating whether the user has given consent for the communication type. It is true if consent is given, otherwise false.

likelyAvailableUserIds.description: An array of strings representing the user IDs of those likely available for the meeting.

locale.description: A string representing the locale of the person booking the meeting.

slug.description: A string representing the unique identifier for the meeting link.

startTime.description: The start time of the meeting in ISO 8601 date-time format.

timezone.description: A string representing the timezone of the person booking the meeting.

actions.name: get_crm_list_by_name
actions.description: Retrieve List by Name. Retrieve a specific list by its name and object type ID. This endpoint allows you to fetch details about a list, including its properties and optionally its filters. It is useful for accessing list information based on specific criteria.

listName.description: The name of the list to fetch. This is **not** case sensitive.

objectTypeId.description: The object type ID of the object types stored by the list to fetch. For example, `0-1` for a `CONTACT` list.

includeFilters.description: A flag indicating whether or not the response object list definition should include a filter branch definition. By default, object list definitions will not have their filter branch definitions included in the response.

actions.name: search_crm_lists
actions.description: Search lists by list name or page through all lists by providing an empty `query` value.

additionalProperties.description:
The property names of any additional list properties to include in the response. Properties that do not exist or that are empty for a particular list are not included in the response.

By default, all requests will fetch the following properties for each list: `hs_list_size`, `hs_last_record_added_at`, `hs_last_record_removed_at`, `hs_folder_name`, and `hs_list_reference_count`.

count.description: The number of lists to include in the response. Defaults to `20` if no value is provided. The max `count` is `500`.

listIds.description: ILS list ids to be included in search results. If not specified, all lists matching other criteria will be included

offset.description: Value used to paginate through lists. The `offset` provided in the response can be used in the next request to fetch the next page of results. Defaults to `0` if no offset is provided.

processingTypes.description: List processing types to be included in search results. If not specified, all lists with all processing types will be included.

query.description: The `query` that will be used to search for lists by list name. If no `query` is provided, then the results will include all lists.

sort.description: Sort field and order

actions.name: delete_crm_list
actions.description: Delete a list by **ILS list ID**. Lists deleted through this endpoint can be restored up to 90-days following the delete. After 90-days, the list is purged and can no longer be restored.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the list to delete.

actions.name: get_segment_members
actions.description:
Fetch List Memberships Ordered by ID. Fetch the memberships of a list in order sorted by the `recordId` of the records in the list.

The `recordId`s are sorted in *ascending* order if an `after` offset or no offset is provided. If only a `before` offset is provided, then the records are sorted in *descending* order.

The `after` offset parameter will take precedence over the `before` offset in a case where both are provided.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the list.

after.description:
The paging offset token for the page that comes `after` the previously requested records.

If provided, then the records in the response will be the records following the offset, sorted in *ascending* order. Takes precedence over the `before` offset.

before.description:
The paging offset token for the page that comes `before` the previously requested records.

If provided, then the records in the response will be the records preceding the offset, sorted in *descending* order.

limit.description: The number of records to return in the response. The maximum `limit` is 250.

actions.name: delete_records_from_list
actions.description:
Delete All Records from a List. Remove **all** of the records from a list. ***Note:*** *The list is not deleted.*

This endpoint only works for lists that have a `processingType` of `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT`.

This endpoint only supports lists that have less than 100,000 memberships.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT` list.

actions.name: add_records_to_list
actions.description:
Add Records to a List. Add the records provided to the list. Records that do not exist or that are already members of the list are ignored.

This endpoint only works for lists that have a `processingType` of `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT`.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT` list.

actions.name: update_list_memberships
actions.description:
Add and/or Remove Records from a List. Add and/or remove records that have already been created in the system to and/or from a list.

This endpoint only works for lists that have a `processingType` of `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT`.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT` list.

actions.name: add_records_from_source_list_to_destination_list
actions.description:
Add All Records from a Source List to a Destination List. Add all of the records from a *source list* (specified by the `sourceListId`) to a *destination list* (specified by the `listId`). Records that are already members of the *destination list* will be ignored. The *destination* and *source list* IDs must be different. The *destination* and *source lists* must contain records of the same type (e.g. contacts, companies, etc.).

This endpoint only works for *destination lists* that have a `processingType` of `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT`. The *source list* can have any `processingType`.

This endpoint only supports a `sourceListId` for lists with less than 100,000 memberships.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT` *destination list*, which the *source list* records are added to.

sourceListId.description: The **ILS ID** of the *source list* to grab the records from, which are then added to the *destination list*.

actions.name: fetch_list_memberships_ordered_by_added_to_list_date
actions.description:
Fetch List Memberships Ordered by Added to List Date. Fetch the memberships of a list in order sorted by the time the records were added to the list.

The `recordId`s are sorted in *ascending* order if an `after` offset or no offset is provided. If only a `before` offset is provided, then the records are sorted in *descending* order.

The `after` offset parameter will take precedence over the `before` offset in a case where both are provided.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the list.

after.description:
The paging offset token for the page that comes `after` the previously requested records.

If provided, then the records in the response will be the records following the offset, sorted in *ascending* order. Takes precedence over the `before` offset.

before.description:
The paging offset token for the page that comes `before` the previously requested records.

If provided, then the records in the response will be the records preceding the offset, sorted in *descending* order.

limit.description: The number of records to return in the response. The maximum `limit` is 250.

actions.name: remove_records_from_list
actions.description:
Remove Records from a List. Remove the records provided from the list. Records that do not exist or that are not members of the list are ignored.

This endpoint only works for lists that have a `processingType` of `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT`.

listId.description: The **ILS ID** of the `MANUAL` or `SNAPSHOT` list.

actions.name: update_form_definition
actions.description: Update a form definition. Update all fields of a hubspot form definition.

allowLinkToResetKnownValues.description: Whether to add a reset link to the form. This removes any pre-populated content on the form and creates a new contact on submission.

archivable.description: Whether the form can be archived.

cloneable.description: Whether the form can be cloned.

createNewContactForNewEmail.description: Whether to create a new contact when a form is submitted with an email address that doesn’t match any in your existing contacts records.

editable.description: Whether the form can be edited.

language.description: The language of the form.

objectTypeId.description: The objectTypeId for both contact and company

value.description: The internal name of the contact's lifecycle stage set when submitting a form

notifyContactOwner.description: Whether to send a notification email to the contact owner when a submission is received.

notifyRecipients.description: The list of user IDs to receive a notification email when a submission is received.

type.description: The action to take after submit. The default action is displaying a thank you message.

value.description: The thank you text or the page to redirect to.

prePopulateKnownValues.description: Whether contact fields should pre-populate with known information when a contact returns to your site.

cssClass.description: Custom CSS class name(s) to apply to the form element for additional styling.

renderRawHtml.description: Whether the form will render as raw HTML as opposed to inside an iFrame.

backgroundWidth.description: The width of the form background. Accepts percentage (e.g., "100%") or pixel values (e.g., "600px").

fontFamily.description: Font family used throughout the form (e.g., "arial, helvetica, sans-serif").

helpTextColor.description: Hex color code for help text displayed below form fields.

helpTextSize.description: Font size for help text. Accepts pixel values (e.g., "11px").

labelTextColor.description: Hex color code for field labels.

labelTextSize.description: Font size for field labels. Accepts pixel values (e.g., "11px").

submitAlignment.description: Horizontal alignment of the submit button. Values: left, center, right.

submitColor.description: Hex color code for the submit button background.

submitFontColor.description: Hex color code for the submit button text.

submitSize.description: Font size for submit button text. Accepts pixel values (e.g., "12px").

submitButtonText.description: The text displayed on the form submit button.

theme.description: The theme used for styling the input fields. This will not apply if the form is added to a HubSpot CMS page.

List duplicate pairs. Returns pairs of records identified as potential duplicates by HubSpot's default detection method. Records are scored by similarity across a standard set of properties. Use objectId to narrow results to pairs containing a specific record. To detect duplicates using custom matching criteria, see the custom duplicate rules endpoints.

By default, HubSpot identifies potential duplicates by comparing record property values for the following properties:

Contacts: First name, Last name, Email address, IP country, Phone number, Zip code, and Company name.
Companies: Company domain name, Company name, Country/Region, Phone number, and Industry.

items.description: Contains an array of CRM object records to be processed in a batch operation, each defined by their ID and properties.

id.description: The id to be updated. This can be the object id, or the unique property value of the idProperty property

idProperty.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object

objectWriteTraceId.description: A unique identifier for tracing the request.

properties.description: Key-value pairs representing the properties of the object.

actions.name: upsert_calls
actions.description: Create or update a batch of calls by unique property values. Create or update records identified by a unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param. `idProperty` query param refers to a property whose values are unique for the object.

inputs.description: An array of simple public objects to be upserted. Each object in the array contains the necessary data for creating or updating a record in HubSpot.

items.description: Represents an object used in batch upsert operations, containing an object’s unique identifier, its properties, and optionally the unique property name and a write trace ID.

id.description: The unique ID of the object.

idProperty.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object

objectWriteTraceId.description: An identifier for tracing the creation request.

properties.description: Key value pairs representing the properties of the object.

actions.name: search_calls
actions.description: Search for calls by filtering on properties, searching through associations, and sorting results. Learn more about [CRM search](https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/guides/api/crm/search#make-a-search-request).

after.description: A paging cursor token for retrieving subsequent pages.

filterGroups.description: Up to 6 groups of filters defining additional query criteria.

items.description: Represents a group of filters used to query data within HubSpot. This component is used to define criteria for filtering records in various API endpoints.

filters.description: A list of individual filter criteria that are applied together as a group. Each filter specifies a condition that records must meet to be included in the results.

items.description: Defines a single condition for searching CRM objects, specifying the property to filter on, the operator to use (such as equals, greater than, or contains), and the value(s) to compare against.

highValue.description: The upper boundary value when using ranged-based filters.

operator.description: The comparison operator used in the filter, such as "EQ" or "GT".

propertyName.description: The name of the property to apply the filter to.

value.description: The value to match against the property.

values.description: The values to match against the property.

limit.description: The maximum results to return, up to 200 objects.

properties.description: A list of property names to include in the response.

query.description: The search query string, up to 3000 characters.

sorts.description: Specifies sorting order based on object properties.

actions.name: read_call
actions.description: Read an Object identified by `{callId}`. `{callId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, or optionally any unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param.  Control what is returned via the `properties` query param.

archived.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

associations.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

idProperty.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

properties.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

propertiesWithHistory.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

actions.name: delete_call
actions.description: Archive. Move an Object identified by `{callId}` to the recycling bin.

actions.name: update_call
actions.description: Update. Perform a partial update of an Object identified by `{callId}`or optionally a unique property value as specified by the `idProperty` query param. `{callId}` refers to the internal object ID by default, and the `idProperty` query param refers to a property whose values are unique for the object. Provided property values will be overwritten. Read-only and non-existent properties will result in an error. Properties values can be cleared by passing an empty string.

idProperty.description: The name of a property whose values are unique for this object type

properties.description: Key value pairs representing the properties of the object.

actions.name: get_url_mappings_url_mappings
actions.description: Get url mappings url mappings.

actions.name: create_url_mappings_url_mappings
actions.description: Create url mappings url mappings.

destination.description: The destination URL, where the target URL should be redirected if it matches the `routePrefix`.

id.description: The unique ID of this URL redirect.

isMatchFullUrl.description: Whether the `routePrefix` should match on the entire URL, including the domain.

isMatchQueryString.description: Whether the `routePrefix` should match on the entire URL path, including the query string.

isOnlyAfterNotFound.description: Whether the URL redirect mapping should apply only if a live page on the URL isn't found. If False, the URL redirect mapping will take precedence over any existing page.

isPattern.description: Whether the `routePrefix` should match based on pattern.

isProtocolAgnostic.description: Whether the `routePrefix` should match both HTTP and HTTPS protocols.

isTrailingSlashOptional.description: Whether a trailing slash will be ignored.

precedence.description: Used to prioritize URL redirection. If a given URL matches more than one redirect, the one with the **lower** precedence will be used.

redirectStyle.description: The type of redirect to create. Options include: 301 (permanent), 302 (temporary), or 305 (proxy). Find more details [here](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/cos-general/how-to-redirect-a-hubspot-page).

routePrefix.description: The target incoming URL, path, or pattern to match for redirection.

actions.name: list_contracts
actions.description: List. Read a page of contracts. Control what is returned via the `properties` query param.

after.description: The paging cursor token of the last successfully read resource will be returned as the `paging.next.after` JSON property of a paged response containing more results.

archived.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

associations.description: A comma separated list of object types to retrieve associated IDs for. If any of the specified associations do not exist, they will be ignored.

limit.description: The maximum number of results to display per page.

properties.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned in the response. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored.

propertiesWithHistory.description: A comma separated list of the properties to be returned along with their history of previous values. If any of the specified properties are not present on the requested object(s), they will be ignored. Usage of this parameter will reduce the maximum number of contracts that can be read by a single request.

actions.name: read_contracts
actions.description: Read a batch of contracts by internal ID, or unique property values. Retrieve records by record ID or include the `idProperty` parameter to retrieve records by a custom unique value property.

archived.description: Whether to return only results that have been archived.

idProperty.description: When using a custom unique value property to retrieve records, the name of the property. Do not include this parameter if retrieving by record ID.

inputs.description: An array of SimplePublicObjectId objects, each containing the ID of an object to be read.

items.description: Contains the Id of a Public Object

id.description: The unique ID of the object.

properties.description: An array of the property names to be returned in the response. If a specified property is not present on the requested object(s), it will be ignored.

propertiesWithHistory.description: An array of the property names to be returned along with their history of previous values. If a specified property is not present on the requested object(s), it will be ignored.
